name: Weighted, provenance-aware cross-platform account graphs

attribution.legal_posture: First-party provider observations and source-attributed investigations supply a public security-research assessment; legal identity, civil identity, adjacent-account control, court findings, labor-market prevalence and independently validated efficacy require separate sources.

ttps: weighted cross-platform identity and repository correlation
caveats: Auto-blocking every neighbor of a flagged account and using demographic or nationality proxies are unsuitable controls.
Identity-document imagery, synthetic-image examples, biometric templates, candidate-level telemetry, and raw graph nodes stay out of publication and operational use.

Graph edges require provenance, weighting, explainability, temporal context, and human review; shared résumé structure, employers, repositories, or contact patterns provide correlation context, while identity proof requires additional evidence.
Identity or attribution requires more than a single face, image, document, VPN, location, device, network, profile, résumé, repository, contact, or behavior signal.
The package includes published Rapid7 graph context only; inferred labels are excluded.
Retain source provenance and confidence for every edge and distinguish shared control from ordinary collaboration.

Successful or failed verification is one bounded observation; legal identity, nationality, DPRK affiliation, worker continuity, present account control and product-wide performance require separate evidence.
The source-labeled 23 additional applicants remain suspicious review leads; worker, incident, and legal identity status remain unconfirmed.
Use explainable multi-signal review, minimization, bounded retention, trained human adjudication, correction, appeal, accessibility accommodations, and applicable legal review.

statements: Useful graph edges include repeated code-repository handles, shared projects/code, social relationships, overlapping email-domain patterns, infrastructure reuse, contractor-profile attributes, and front-company accounts. Human review should distinguish a true shared-control signal from ordinary open-source collaboration.

sources.support: Pindrop says one confirmed fraud case led it to 23 additional suspicious applicants through repeated resume structure, recurring claimed employers, reused or swapped repositories, and contact-pattern overlap. This is useful first-party hiring-pipeline provenance for the existing weighted, provenance-aware graph-control record. Evidence boundary: Provider-reported observations from Pindrop's own pipeline. The article does not publish methodology sufficient to reproduce its labels, cohort sizes for every percentage, independent validation, named candidates, legal identities, or a labor-market prevalence estimate. Its 'confirmed fraud' and 'linked to North Korea' labels are source labels, not adjudications
